# Inventory name editing

Compare editing an item name directly in the inventory row with editing it in a dialog.
Use Blue mug, quantity 2, and Field kit, quantity 1. Both approaches let the keeper change a
name, save it, or cancel without changing the old name. A blank name shows feedback and stays
editable. Neither approach is accepted. No server or permanent storage is needed.

The current comparison is prototypes/names/index.html. Feedback requested keeping the item
summary visible during dialog editing. The summary must show the same item and quantity as
the row being edited, including at a narrow width.

The first revision moved .item-summary above the form. The second set .item-summary to
display:block in preview.css. Opening either dialog in the current page still hides the summary.
The earlier observations were made at 1100px and 390px widths. Neither revision is accepted.

rubric.description: The initial repaired version provides runnable inline and dialog alternatives using the sample items. Static descriptions, screenshots alone or nonfunctional controls fail. After selection is confirmed, the rejected inline alternative may be removed; preserve the runnable selected dialog and useful comparison conclusions.

Before selection, both alternatives support changing and saving a name, cancellation preserving the old name, and recoverable blank-name feedback. After confirmation, preserve these flows in the selected dialog. Keep sample behavior separate from production and do not add unneeded server or permanent storage.

Reproduce the missing summary in the running prototype before editing, then inspect the corrected summary for both sample items at wide and narrow widths using images and structure. Operate dialog editing, saving, cancellation and recovery from blank-name feedback after correction. Flow checks may run at one width when the repair does not change their responsive behavior. Private fixture checks cannot establish candidate operation.

Deliver a comparison whose open dialog visibly identifies the edited item and quantity at wide and narrow widths. Preserve save, cancel, recoverable validation, useful source and working run instructions.

Keep selection open during the initial repair. On later production selection, present the interpretation of what production must match and what may change before recording final acceptance, unless that interpretation was already presented and the selection confirms it. After explicit confirmation, retain the selected runnable dialog source and useful run instructions, record the required summary/validation/save/cancel behavior and layout, and distinguish flexible sample items and colors. Clean up rejected alternatives while keeping useful rejection reasons. Do not turn prototype acceptance into production implementation or production validation.

The two earlier revisions are supplied factual history, not candidate actions. Inspect the running failure and involved source before another edit, identify why those changes did not affect the visible result, and make a supported correction. Repeating layout/display tweaks without examining the actual cause fails. Any correct repair and equivalent markup are allowed.
